I have a couple of questions about policy.  Because I am a newcomer to this endeavor, and because I can also be a stuffed shirt, and because this is a community project and I have no right to force my standards upon the community, I ask these questions:

1.)  This was a first-person report on an event.  I corrected obvious mistakes such as run on words (like ''hewas'').  What is the policy about the kind of entry when the user makes a spelling error that cannot be determined to be a typo (I refer here to ''Ghoul'')?  In one sense were I to correct it, I would be tampering IMHO, with the essence of the contribution.  I know, the issue is a little esoteric, but I'd rather check first than start a flame war.

2.)  The author refers at one point to ''kick ass sa'angreal''.  If we aspire to a modicum of professionalism, does such a phrase have any place in this work?
[[User:Pedantic|Pedantic]] 19:32, 20 February 2008 (UTC)

:While your policy question is valid, I have a better one.  This article has no actual question asked of RJ, and no actual answer from RJ.  It is a journal entry that boils down to "I went to the book signing and it was fun".  Does this Article even deserve to be in the Wiki at all? 
:That said kick ass Sa'angreal was part of a quote and shouldn't be modified, however linking it to [[Choedan Kal]] would be fair. I would also say as the source is spoken any spelling error is a typo and should be fixed. [[User:Melriken|Melriken]] 21:31, 20 February 2008 (UTC)
